## Bio

I am a Ph.D. Candidate in Business Artificial Intelligence at the School of Management, Fudan University, advised by Professor Tianjun Feng. My research focuses on human-AI work allocation and decision authority in service operations.

I study how generative AI, AI agents, and human-AI collaboration reshape work in service systems and digital platforms. I use field experiments, causal inference, machine learning, and LLM-based text analysis to examine how operational decisions and the allocation of work between humans and AI affect service performance.

My current research is also grounded in industry collaboration, especially in customer service and platform contexts where AI systems interact with workers, customers, and organizational decision rules.

:::

::: {.content-band}
## Research Focus

My research focuses on human-AI work design and decision authority, AI-enabled service systems and digital platforms, and the allocation of front-office communication and back-office problem-solving effort in service operations.

::: {.stream-grid}
::: {.stream-card}
### GenAI and Service Operations

How GenAI changes customer service workflows, service quality, escalation, and recovery in customer service and contact-center operations.
:::

::: {.stream-card}
### AI Agents and Platform Operations

How agentic AI systems operate inside platform-mediated service environments, including customer service operations and online service platforms.
:::

::: {.stream-card}
### Human-AI Collaboration

Human-in-the-loop intervention, escalation timing, AI failure recovery, and worker effort in hybrid service systems.
:::
:::
:::

## Selected Working Papers

<div class="paper-meta">(Job Market paper, *co-first authorship), major revision at <em>Operations Research</em></div>

### Agentic AI and Human-in-the-Loop Interventions: Field Experimental Evidence from Alibaba's Customer Service Operations

Yiwei Wang\*, **Chuan Zhu**\*, Tianjun Feng, Lauren Xiaoyuan Lu, and Bingxin Jia.

- **Finalist, 2026 INFORMS Service Science Best Student Paper Competition.**
- **Best Paper Nominee, CIST 2026.**

This paper uses a randomized field experiment involving 647 workers and approximately 681,000 customer-service chats at Alibaba Taobao. Agentic AI reduces average chat duration but may lower customer ratings. Descriptive post-escalation analyses show more favorable outcomes after technical than emotional escalations, with differences in intervention timing and human effort.

::: {.paper-links}
[arXiv abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14830)
[SSRN author page](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/cf_dev/AbsByAuth.cfm?per_id=11527448)
[Paper PDF](<papers/Agentic AI and Human-in-the-Loop Interventions_2026-0511_corrected-original.pdf>)
:::
:::

::: {.paper-entry}
<div class="paper-meta">Working paper</div>

### Talk the Talk and Walk the Walk: An Empirical Study of Front-Office Communication and Back-Office Problem Solving Under Workload Pressure

**Chuan Zhu**, Tom Fangyun Tan, and Tianjun Feng.

Using 3,965,028 live-chat sessions handled by 7,004 agents, this paper identifies within-session effort allocation as a mechanism linking workload to service performance. Workload has a U-shaped relationship with the share of effort devoted to customer communication. Counterfactual estimates suggest that rebalancing communication and back-office problem solving can shorten sessions, improve customer ratings, and reduce retrials without adding capacity.

:::
